description: This pie chart, from the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models,” visually represents the distribution of categories across which a model’s attribution was evaluated, with each slice corresponding to a specific domain and its percentage share. The chart contains ten distinct slices, each labeled with its category name and percentage. The largest segment is “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, shown in blue. The second largest is “Econ. & Fin.” at 18.4%, depicted in teal. “Daily Life” accounts for 7.1% (light blue-green), “History” for 8.2% (yellow), “Game&Anime” for 8.2% (orange), “Law” for 5.1% (pinkish-red), “Science” for 6.7% (light blue), “Med & Health” for 5.5% (green), “Pet & Animal” for 5.5% (orange), “Business” for 5.9% (red), and “Math” for 1.2% (dark green). The chart includes a legend that associates each category with its color and percentage, and the percentages are explicitly labeled next to each corresponding slice. The slices are arranged in a roughly descending order by size, starting from the largest at the top right and proceeding clockwise. There is no visual emphasis such as exploded slices or bolding.
